title: Blank world map
subject: Geography
unit: Spring 1: Earning a living and globalisation
source: Written for geography/y9 lesson 12 (Blank world map (portal printable))
intro: Lesson 12. Use it to map the countries in the lesson.

blocks.caption: Outline from Natural Earth (public domain); modern coastlines and borders.

questions.q: Trace a phone's supply chain in four steps.
questions.a: Minerals mined (for example cobalt in DR Congo), chips made (Taiwan), assembled (China), sold in the UK
questions.model: Start in the ground: minerals mined. Then parts: chips made. Then put together: assembly. Then to us: shipped and sold.

questions.q: Give one benefit of globalisation for the UK.
questions.a: Cheaper goods, or jobs from foreign companies investing

questions.q: Core: Draw a world map of a phone's supply chain with at least five labelled stages and arrows.
questions.a: Map showing mining in DR Congo, chips in Taiwan or South Korea, assembly in China or India, shipping, sale in the UK
questions.model: Teacher shows it first: arrow from DR Congo labelled 'cobalt mined' to China labelled 'battery made and phone assembled'.

questions.q: Extend: In the portal response box, write two paragraphs: who wins and who loses from globalisation?
questions.a: Winners: consumers, TNCs, some workers in new factories. Losers: miners in unsafe conditions, workers in closed UK factories; environment

questions.q: Stretch: How could buyers make phones more ethical?
questions.a: Buy fewer and keep them longer, recycle, choose firms that check their supply chains

questions.q: Most of the world's mined cobalt comes from:
Big question: how many countries does it take to make one mobile phone?
questions.a: Many: minerals, parts, assembly and sales happen in different countries across the world
